You are a data-acquisition subagent for the research agent "claude", which is building a 3D MHD solar-wind model to estimate the solar-wind proton/heavy-ion flux at interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS (C/2025 N1) during its XMM-Newton observation, 2025-12-03T12:04:07 to 2025-12-04T10:11:54 UTC (comet at about 1.88 AU). Work fully autonomously: no human will answer questions. Make sensible calls, then report what you decided.

WORKSPACE (write only here): /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/data/ (create subfolders ephem/, insitu/, qc/). Never write into other agents' folders (mhd_llm/argon, mhd_llm/codex) or into mhd_llm/shared_notes. Read-only reference material: the preprint text at mhd_llm/claude/ref/main.txt, and the preprint's solar-wind task at /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/analysis_repro/analysis_06_solar_wind/ (solar_wind.py, plus cache/ holding the hourly STA/SolO/ACE/Wind CSVs and Horizons tracks it used, Nov 8–Dec 30 2025).

RESOURCES: the machine is shared by three agents. Use at most 4 CPU threads, at most 3 GB RAM, and no GPU. Wrap any heavy Python in `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=3G <cmd>`. Python: base env /home/scabot/miniconda3/bin/python3 (numpy, scipy, astropy, astroquery, pandas, cdflib, matplotlib). A second env, /home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python, is being built now (it adds sunpy, numba, h5py); use it for frame transforms once it exists, and fall back to your own implementation if it never appears. Run Python that parses downloaded files with `-I`. Store downloads separately from your scripts: scripts go in data/scripts/.

CODE STYLE (user mandate): minimal and parsimonious, with no comments and no docstrings in code, and no free-text "note" fields inside output JSON/CSV. Put deviations and caveats in a README.md instead. Use American spelling.

TASKS
1. Ephemerides, hourly, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-20 UTC, from JPL Horizons (astroquery or the API https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), for: 3I/ATLAS (try id "C/2025 N1" or the designation that resolves to the comet; the preprint code used id "C/2025 N1" with id_type=None), Earth (399), STEREO-A (-234), Solar Orbiter (-144), Parker Solar Probe (-96), BepiColombo (-121), Mars (499), MAVEN (-202), Venus (299), Mercury (199), JUICE (-28), Psyche (-255), Europa Clipper (-159). For each body write data/ephem/<name>.csv with columns: utc (ISO), x_hci_km, y_hci_km, z_hci_km, r_au, hgi_lon_deg, hgi_lat_deg (heliocentric inertial, solar-equator based; this is the HCI frame of sunpy/Thompson 2006), carr_lon_deg, carr_lat_deg (Carrington, heliographic), heeq_lon_deg, heeq_lat_deg (Stonyhurst), vx_hci, vy_hci, vz_hci (km/s), and also ecl_lon_deg (heliocentric ecliptic J2000, the convention the preprint used). Compute the transforms with sunpy if available. Otherwise implement HCI/Carrington from the IAU solar pole (RA 286.13°, Dec 63.87°) and the Carrington prime meridian, and verify against Horizons body-fixed output (center @sun, refplane body) or sunpy for a few epochs, documenting the check. Use light-time-free geometric positions; that is fine at our accuracy. Report the comet's r, HGI/Carrington/HEEQ longitude and latitude, and its HCI velocity (radial and tangential components) at the observation midpoint, plus its longitude separation from Earth, STEREO-A, SolO, PSP, and Mars.
2. In-situ solar wind, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-20, via CDAWeb HAPI (https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/hapi; use /catalog and /info to confirm dataset IDs and parameter names; retry on transient errors). Highest priority first:
   a) OMNI at L1: OMNI_HRO2_5MIN (or OMNI_HRO_5MIN) and OMNI2_H0_MRG1HR: proton density, flow speed, Vx/Vy/Vz, temperature, |B|, Bx/By/Bz (GSE), and the spacecraft ID flags.
   b) STEREO-A PLASTIC: the 1-min L2 proton moments (e.g. STA_L2_PLA_1DMAX_1MIN or the current equivalent) plus the hourly STA_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA (density, speed, temperature, B, and its RTN components if present).
   c) Solar Orbiter: SWA-PAS ground moments (e.g. SOLO_L2_SWA-PAS-GRND-MOM) and SOLO_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA. Also SWA-HIS composition (C/O, O7+/O6+, Fe/O, if available for Oct–Dec 2025, e.g. SOLO_L3_SWA-HIS-COMP-10MIN) and MAG (RTN, 1-min or hourly).
   d) Parker Solar Probe: SWEAP SPAN-I L3 moments (PSP_SWP_SPI_SF00_L3_MOM) and/or SPC L3 (PSP_SWP_SPC_L3I), plus FIELDS MAG if easy. Record which date ranges are available; PSP had a perihelion around 2025-12-12.
   e) ACE: SWEPAM (AC_H0_SWE if a level-2 version now exists for late 2025; otherwise AC_K1_SWE), and SWICS composition (O7+/O6+, C6+/C5+, Fe/O; e.g. AC_H3_SW2 or AC_H6_SWI) for Oct–Dec 2025.
   f) Wind SWE (WI_H1_SWE or WI_K0_SWE) and DSCOVR Faraday cup if available on CDAWeb.
   g) MAVEN SWIA upstream solar-wind moments at Mars (e.g. MVN_SWI_L2_ONBOARDSVYMOM), if public for this period. Note that Mars was approaching solar conjunction.
   Save each as data/insitu/<mission>_<product>.csv with a utc column and physical columns in standard units (n cm^-3, v km/s, T K, B nT). Replace fill values with NaN, and keep data quality flags as columns where they exist. Also make hourly-averaged versions data/insitu/hourly_<mission>.csv with columns utc,n,v,T,B,vr (and composition columns where available), produced by consistent 1-hour bin means that require ≥50% coverage.
3. Cross-check your hourly STEREO-A, SolO, ACE, and Wind series against the preprint's cached CSVs in analysis_06_solar_wind/cache/ over their overlap and report any discrepancies (they should agree closely).
4. QC: write PNGs to data/qc/: (i) a top-down HCI x–y plot of all trajectories for Nov 15–Dec 10 with the comet path and markers at 2025-12-03T23:00; (ii) multi-panel time series of n, v, and n·v for every spacecraft over Oct 15–Dec 15, with the XMM window shaded; (iii) coverage bars.
5. Write data/README.md (sources, dataset IDs, parameters, time spans, gaps, caveats such as preliminary ACE density, and frame definitions), and data/inventory.json (machine-readable: file, mission, product, cadence, t_start, t_end, n_valid).

FINAL REPLY (keep it compact, since it goes back to the main agent): the list of files written; the comet's geometry at mid-observation (r, all longitudes and latitudes, velocity components, separations); the coverage of each spacecraft over Nov 15–Dec 10; the result of the cross-check against the preprint caches; anything missing or surprising.

Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.

# Analysis 06: solar wind and PN light curve

## Run

```bash
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/xmm/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}
/home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/xmm/bin/python run.py
```

Inputs are the cached solar-wind series and the eight masked PN event and OoT
files, GTIs, ephemeris, attitude, calibration index, and ODF summary.

Outputs are `mapped_flux.tsv`, `lightcurve.tsv`, `result.json`, and Figure 4 as
PNG and PDF.

## Method

The hourly inputs are STEREO-A `STA_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA`, Solar Orbiter
`SOLO_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA`, ACE `AC_K1_SWE`, and Wind
`OMNI2_H0_MRG1HR`; OMNI spacecraft code 52 selects Wind. Horizons tracks use
3I/ATLAS, STEREO-A (`-234`), Solar Orbiter (`-144`), ACE (`-92`), and Earth
(`399`). OMNI times already represent arrival near Earth.

Each monitor sample is mapped by

`t_a = t_s + wrap180(lambda_c(t_a)-lambda_m(t_s))/14.1844 + (r_c(t_a)-r_m(t_s))*AU/v`

and its flux is scaled by `(r_m/r_c)^2`. Gaps over 1.5 hours remain empty;
segments are sampled every 10 minutes and averaged in a centered 120-minute
window. ACE density uses a fixed factor of 1.7 relative to Wind; the unscaled
series is omitted from the relative panel. The Parker panel uses the nearest
STEREO-A hourly sample within the 1.5-hour gap limit.

F10.7 is the Penticton 20:00 UT value adjusted to 1 au. `F10.7A` is its centered
81-day mean and `F10.7P=(F10.7+F10.7A)/2`; Task 08 uses the mean F10.7P of the
two observation dates. The adopted ion-fraction range is `3e-4--1e-3`, from
Schwadron--Cravens, ACE/SWICS, and Solar Orbiter/HIS. The heavy-ion number-flux
prior is the zero-truncated `N(1.0e5, 3.8e4)` cm^-2 s^-1 distribution.

The light curve selects 200--1000 eV PN singles (`PATTERN==0`, `FLAG==0`). The
15 common 45-arcsec source holes apply to events, OoT events, and exposure. SAS
`eexpmap` is unvignetted (`VIGNET=F`) and includes filter transmission, quantum
efficiency, GTIs, gaps, and bad pixels. For every frame,

`rate = A370[(Nsrc-0.063 Osrc)/Esrc - (Nbg-0.063 Obg)/Ebg]`,

where `A370=pi(370/60)^2` arcmin2 and the background annulus is 480--720
arcsec.

Primary documentation: [CDAWeb HAPI](https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/hapi),
[OMNI timing](https://omniweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/html/sc_merge_data1.html),
[Horizons](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/manual.html),
[Penticton F10.7](https://www.spaceweather.gc.ca/forecast-prevision/solar-solaire/solarflux/sx-5-en.php),
[SAS eexpmap](https://xmm-tools.cosmos.esa.int/external/sas/current/doc/eexpmap/node3.html),
[Schwadron & Cravens (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1086/317176), and
[Koutroumpa et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024GL114374), with the
[Solar Orbiter HIS archive](https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/misc/NotesS.html).

def write_tsv(path, columns, rows):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)


def read_tsv(path):

def fetch(url, path):
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size:
        return path.read_text()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, headers={"User-Agent": "3I-ATLAS-reproduction"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=180) as response:
        text = response.read().decode()
    temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    temporary.write_text(text)
    temporary.replace(path)
    return text
